canonicalSource.note: The design canon lives in this repository at myne-agents/docs/design/. Token values in DESIGN.md and DESIGN.json are extracted from myne-agents/docs/design/colors_and_type.css, which is the CSS-variable source and therefore the binding value. When that file and these values disagree, the CSS wins and this projection gets corrected.

categoricalPalette.purpose: Eight decorative node-dot colors for the graph pane's color-group feature (graph-connection-ux-polish). Read side by side at small node radius, so legibility is a property of the set: hues stay clear of the three state roles above (never confusable with an error/warning/success color) and alternate lightness band per hue so adjacent colors stay distinguishable under red-green color-vision deficiency, not by hue alone. Source of truth is client-core/src/tokens.css (light + dark + amoled, the amoled twin reusing the dark value verbatim); myne-agents/docs/design/colors_and_type.css mirrors light + dark.

display.purpose: Hero headlines on marketing-adjacent surfaces only.

headline.purpose: Welcome screen sections, vault-creation step headings.

body.purpose: Desktop client default at 14px. Sustained reading.

body-large.purpose: Onboarding copy and recovery-flow prose where the message must land carefully.

caption.purpose: Captions, helper text, status text in ink-tertiary.

label.purpose: The only uppercase role in the system. Used for eyebrow tags above primary blocks.

mono.purpose: Code spans, fingerprints, file paths. Never used for prose.

account-number.purpose: Signature treatment for MY-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX — 27 characters, the MY- prefix plus five 4-char Crockford groups (myne-agents/docs/spec/account-number.md §2). Always non-breaking hyphens, user-select all, slashed zero on.

shadows.name: shadow-3
shadows.purpose: Command palette and modal dialogs only.

shadows.name: shadow-2-dark
shadows.purpose: Dropdown menus and toasts, dark theme.

shadows.name: shadow-3-dark
shadows.purpose: Command palette and modal dialogs, dark theme.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: UI transitions: panel open, palette show.

motion.name: duration-slow
motion.purpose: Modal enter and substantial state changes.

motion.name: duration-instant
motion.purpose: EXPRESSIVE tier. Press/pointer-down feedback. Anything slower reads as the control deciding whether to respond.

motion.name: duration-slower
motion.purpose: EXPRESSIVE tier. The one duration above the 300ms UI ceiling; legitimate only for a large surface or a shared-element travel. Named so a reviewer has to notice it.

motion.name: ease-emphasized
motion.purpose: EXPRESSIVE tier. Emphasized decelerate: leaves fast, settles slow. For an entrance that should land with weight.

motion.name: ease-spring
motion.value: linear(...) sampled spring, falling back to ease-emphasized
motion.purpose: EXPRESSIVE tier. ~4% overshoot, settles by ~380ms. Declared as --ease-emphasized in :root and upgraded inside @supports (transition-timing-function: linear(0,1)), so a WebView without linear() degrades to a strong decelerate rather than to the CSS-initial ease (an ease-IN-out, the one curve an entrance may not use).

motion.name: stagger-step
motion.purpose: EXPRESSIVE tier. Per-item delay in a cascade. Multiply by index, then clamp to --stagger-max.

motion.name: stagger-max
motion.purpose: EXPRESSIVE tier. HARD cap on total stagger, so a 40-row list cascades over 120ms rather than 720ms.

motion.name: control-pad-y
motion.purpose: Control geometry: vertical padding of a text button.

motion.name: control-pad-x
motion.purpose: Control geometry: horizontal padding of a text button.

motion.name: control-gap
motion.purpose: Control geometry: gap between a button's glyph and its label.

motion.name: field-pad-y
motion.purpose: Control geometry: vertical padding of a text field.

motion.name: field-pad-x
motion.purpose: Control geometry: horizontal padding of a text field.

motion.name: segment-pad-y
motion.purpose: Control geometry: vertical padding of a segmented-control segment.

motion.name: segment-pad-x
motion.purpose: Control geometry: horizontal padding of a segmented-control segment.

focus.name: ring
focus.purpose: Standard focus-visible ring: 2px iron-blue stroke with 1px paper offset. Always visible, never removed.

focus.name: ring-inset
focus.purpose: Inset variant for tight rows where an outer ring would clip.

breakpoints.name: desktop
breakpoints.purpose: Reference desktop viewport; the width every desktop screen is composed against.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The iron-blue workhorse for submit, confirm, and continue actions. Used for the only call-to-action in any region.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #2c4a7a; color: #ffffff; font-family: 'Inter', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.5; padding: 10px 16px; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #233b62; } .ds-btn-primary:active { background: #1b2e4d; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 2px rgba(11,11,9,0.12); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 0; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #fbfbfa, 0 0 0 4px #2c4a7a; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Warm-paper button with hairline border. Used for neutral or destructive secondary actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: #fbfbfa; color: #1a1a17; font-family: 'Inter', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.5; padding: 10px 16px; border: 1px solid #e3e2dd; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #ecebe7; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 0; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #fbfbfa, 0 0 0 4px #2c4a7a; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Default text field with hairline border and an iron-blue focus ring (the border itself does not change color on focus).
components.css: .ds-input-text { background: #fbfbfa; color: #1a1a17; font-family: 'Inter', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.5; padding: 8px 12px; border: 1px solid #c8c7c1; border-radius: 3px; transition: border-color 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1); } .ds-input-text::placeholder { color: #6b6a64; } .ds-input-text:focus-visible { outline: 0; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #fbfbfa, 0 0 0 4px #2c4a7a; } .ds-input-text:disabled { opacity: 0.4; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Flat warm-paper card with a hairline border. Never floats. Never has a colored left-border accent.
components.html:
Recovery phrase
Twenty-four words, written down once.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #f4f4f2; color: #1a1a17; border: 1px solid #e3e2dd; border-radius: 6px; padding: 16px; font-family: 'Inter', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-card-eyebrow { font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.5; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #6b6a64; margin-bottom: 8px; } .ds-card-body { font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.5; color: #1a1a17; }

components.name: Account Number
components.description: Signature crypto-identifier rendering. Always JetBrains Mono medium 16px with slashed zero on, non-breaking hyphens, full-value selection.
components.css: .ds-account-number { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.4; letter-spacing: 0.04em; font-feature-settings: 'ss02', 'zero', 'calt'; color: #1a1a17; background: #f4f4f2; padding: 4px 8px; border-radius: 3px; white-space: nowrap; user-select: all; cursor: text; }

components.name: Sidebar Item
components.description: 32px-tall sidebar row. Iron-blue-soft background is the only place iron-blue appears as a fill outside of primary buttons.
components.html: Architecture notes
components.css: .ds-sidebar-item { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; height: 32px; padding: 8px 12px; border-radius: 3px; background: #fbfbfa; color: #3a3934; font-family: 'Inter', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1; text-decoration: none; transition: background 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1), color 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1); } .ds-sidebar-item:hover { background: #ecebe7; color: #1a1a17; } .ds-sidebar-item--active { background: #e8edf5; color: #2c4a7a; }

components.name: Status Pill
components.description: State communicated by an icon and label, never by the pill background. The pill itself stays neutral.
components.html: Sync error
components.css: .ds-status-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; background: #f4f4f2; color: #6b6a64; font-family: 'Inter', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.5; padding: 2px 10px; border-radius: 999px; }

narrative.overview:
The reference points are a printed page and a Unix terminal, not a SaaS dashboard. The surface is warm off-white paper (#fbfbfa) with warm-shifted near-black ink (#1a1a17). The cryptographic identifiers (account numbers, recovery-phrase words, key fingerprints) render in JetBrains Mono with the slashed zero turned on, because a person will read them aloud, type them by hand, and compare them against another device. The two registers (writerly paper, exact terminal) live in the same window without one swallowing the other.

The system is monochrome by default. More than 90% of any screen is neutral. There is exactly one accent color, an iron-blue #2c4a7a lifted toward sky tones in dark mode (#8aa4d0), and it is used only for focus rings, primary actions, links, the active selection in the sidebar, and the tone of an agent review card's own state while it waits on the reader and once something has landed. State colors (a brick-red danger, a forest-green success, an ochre warning) are muted enough to read as information rather than alarm. The product is built to be lived in for hours: comfortable density, zero looping animations, no marching ants on the focus border, no pulsing status indicators. A user who has been writing for an hour should not have noticed the chrome.

The system explicitly rejects the privacy-product visual canon. There is no lock icon, no shield icon, no green checkmark badge. The Myne mark is a minimal M glyph, not a padlock. There is no glassmorphism, no backdrop-filter, no gradient on text or backgrounds. There are no cards with a colored left-border accent, no hero-metric template, no identical card grids, no stock photography of people. The visual surface for a privacy product should not telegraph that the product is about privacy; that conflation is what the system refuses.
keyCharacteristics: Warm-paper light theme (#fbfbfa) with a dim-paper dark theme (#121210); both first-class.
One accent (iron-blue) used on roughly 5% of any screen; never decorative, never gradient.
Inter Variable for UI sans, JetBrains Mono Variable for cryptographic identifiers (slashed zero on, ss02 + zero + calt).
1px hairlines (#e3e2dd) for every divider; 2px borders are forbidden.
Flat at rest. Shadows live only on overlays (command palette, dropdowns, toasts, tooltips), never on the editor surface or on cards.
Restrained motion: 120/180/260ms, exponential ease-out only, prefers-reduced-motion disables transitions globally.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Iron-blue is the only chromatic color in any UI region except a state surface. Anywhere you reach for 'another color for visual interest', you are wrong; reach for typography, density, or whitespace instead.

rules.name: The Anti-Privacy-Theme Rule
rules.body: No lock icon, no shield icon, no green checkmark badge anywhere on the product surface. Encryption status is communicated typographically (a small caption 'Encrypted, synced 12s ago' in ink-tertiary), never with chrome.

rules.name: The Warm-Black Rule
rules.body: Use #1a1a17, never #000. Use #fbfbfa, never #fff. The 1% chroma toward warm shifts the surface from 'screen' to 'paper' and is the single most identity-defining choice in the system.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Crypto Rule
rules.body: Every value a human types or compares by eye, account numbers, recovery-phrase words, key fingerprints, hash prefixes, file paths, renders in JetBrains Mono with ss02 and zero on. Sans-serif is forbidden for these identifiers because the slashed zero is load-bearing for hand-typed Crockford-base32.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: Buttons, headings, menu items, modal titles: sentence case. 'Save note', not 'Save Note'. Title case is reserved for proper nouns (Myne, Argon2id, BIP-39, XChaCha20-Poly1305, Crockford-base32, Tauri). Acronyms stay in caps (E2EE, AEAD, KDF, AAD).

rules.name: The No-Hype-Words Rule
rules.body: 'Military-grade', 'bank-level', 'unbreakable', 'ultra-secure', 'next-gen': forbidden in every type role. The threat model speaks for the product; marketing language inserted into the type system would expose the system as advertising rather than tooling.

rules.name: The Flat-Editor Rule
rules.body: The editor surface and any pane inside the editor (sidebar, backlinks pane, status bar) carry no shadow. Adding a shadow to a pane is a category error; the editor is paper, and paper does not float over itself.

rules.name: The No-Glass Rule
rules.body: No backdrop-filter, no filter: blur(), no vibrancy, no glassmorphism. Tauri 2 supports it on macOS; the system declines on purpose. The only translucent surface in the entire product is the modal scrim, and it has no blur.

rules.name: The No-Card-Stripe Rule
rules.body: A card is never communicated by a colored left-border accent. Cards earn distinction from the --paper-2 fill and the --line-1 hairline only. If a card needs to communicate state, an eyebrow label inside does the work.

dos: Do treat myne-agents/docs/design/ as the canonical design source, and bind every component to the CSS variables in myne-agents/docs/design/colors_and_type.css rather than to a literal. When a shipped screen and the canon disagree, fix whichever side is actually wrong, and update myne-agents/docs/design/ in the same change when it is the canon that has fallen behind.

Do use OKLCH-style descriptive names in token discussions ('warm paper', 'iron blue', 'brick danger') rather than hex-code references in copy. The hex values are normative; the names are what humans use.
Do render every cryptographic identifier (account numbers, recovery-phrase words, key fingerprints, hash prefixes) in JetBrains Mono with ss02 and zero features on.
Do use the standard 2px iron-blue ring with a 1px paper offset for :focus-visible on every interactive element. The ring is always visible; never removed.
Do use sentence case everywhere. 'Save note', not 'Save Note'. Title case is reserved for proper nouns (Myne, Argon2id, BIP-39, XChaCha20-Poly1305, Crockford-base32, Tauri).
Do communicate state with an icon plus a text label, never with color alone.
Do keep motion under 260ms with exponential ease-out cubic curves. Disable transitions globally under prefers-reduced-motion.

Do ship border-radius: 6px on buttons and cards as the workhorse; 3px on inputs and on chips outside the editor; 10px on the command palette and modals; pill on status pills and on inline editor chips (the MYND-614 exception: an inline chip sits in a line of prose beside the shipped #tag chip, which already uses pill radius).
Do keep neutrals warm-shifted: #fbfbfa not #fff, #1a1a17 not #000. The 1% chroma is identity-defining.
donts: Don't use a lock icon, shield icon, or green checkmark badge anywhere on the product surface. The Myne mark is not a padlock; encryption status is typography, not chrome.
Don't ship a card with a colored left-border accent. Banned outright; full border or nothing.
Don't use backdrop-filter, filter: blur(), vibrancy, or glassmorphism on any surface. The only translucent element in the product is the modal scrim, and it has no blur.
Don't apply gradients to text or backgrounds. Single solid colors only; emphasis via weight and size.
Don't ship a hero-metric SaaS template (big number + small label + supporting stats + gradient accent). Cliché, banned.
Don't ship identical card grids of 'icon + heading + paragraph' repeated endlessly.
Don't ship stock photography of people: hands on keyboards, 'diverse team in glass conference room', smiling laptop owners. None of it.
Don't use emoji as iconography in the product. Lucide stroke icons only, currentColor.
Don't write 'military-grade', 'bank-level', 'unbreakable', 'ultra-secure', 'next-gen' anywhere in the type system. Hype words are forbidden across every surface.
Don't write 'Welcome back, friend!' or 'Connecting securely...' copy. The voice is 'careful engineer to careful engineer', not privacy salesperson.
Don't use looping animations: no pulsing encrypted-status indicator, no marching-ants focus border, no spring physics, no bouncing easings. The product is calm, never twitchy.
Don't add a shadow to the editor surface or to a pane inside the editor. Shadows are reserved for transient overlays (command palette, dropdowns, toasts, tooltips).
Don't use #000 or #fff literally. Always tint toward the warm neutral ramp.
Don't reach for a modal as the first interaction pattern. Inline and progressive alternatives first; modals only when there is genuinely no other shape.
